nodes.summary: MAXIMUM INDUCED MATCHING is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a maximum-induced-matching instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and feasible: the edge list $E$ has no repeated entries, every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$ with $(v, u)$ not in $E$, and some sublist $M$ of $E$ of length at least $K$…
nodes.title: The MAXIMUM INDUCED MATCHING decision problem

nodes.summary: A maximum-induced-matching instance $(n, E, K)$, with vertex count $n$, edge list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers and bound $K$, is feasible when there is a sublist $M$ of $E$ of length at least $K$ such that any two distinct pairs in $M$ share no endpoint, and no pair in $E$ joins an endpoint of one pair in $M$ to an endpoint of a different pair in $M$.
nodes.title: Feasible maximum-induced-matching instances

nodes.summary: A maximum-induced-matching instance is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the vertex count), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).
nodes.title: Maximum-induced-matching instances

nodes.summary: The MAXIMUM INDUCED MATCHING decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM INDUCED MATCHING is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A maximum-induced-matching instance $(n, E, K)$ is well formed when the edge list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, with the reverse pair $(v, u)$ not in $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed maximum-induced-matching instances
